article_title: Effects of a Generative AI Virtual Patient on Serious Illness Communication Skills: Randomized Controlled Trial.
citation: Haut KG, Hasan M, Carroll T, Epstein RM, Sen T, Hoque E. (2026). Effects of a Generative AI Virtual Patient on Serious Illness Communication Skills: Randomized Controlled Trial. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/93034
title: MVP framework and 3E communication skills for serious illness conversations
description: The MVP (medical situation, values, and plan) communication framework and its 3 core skills—Empathize, Be Explicit, and Empower (3Es)—ground both the SOPHIE system and the study's outcome measures. The Empathize skill focuses on responding to emotional distress, Be Explicit on clearly communicating prognosis and uncertainty, and Empower on eliciting values and supporting a patient-centered care plan. The framework was converted into a structured Likert-scale questionnaire to quantify communication behaviors on a numeric scale, normalized to between 0 and 1.
requirements: Raters must be trained on the rubric to produce consistent scores
constraints: The rubric was intended to capture within-participant improvement from before to after the intervention, not to define an ideal level of performance or estimate population-level clinical competence
target_learners: Medical, nursing, and physician assistant students
target_learning_goals: Serious illness communication skills (Empathize, Be Explicit, Empower)
examples: Used as the primary outcome framework: SPs and 4 blinded raters evaluated participants pre- and postintervention using a rubric based on this framework
key_sources: Haut KG, Hasan M, Carroll T, Epstein RM, Sen T, Hoque E. (2026). Effects of a Generative AI Virtual Patient on Serious Illness Communication Skills: Randomized Controlled Trial. JMIR Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.2196/93034

article_title: Impact of a Competency-based Mechanical Ventilation Course Using Virtual Simulation.
citation: Rocha de Macedo Bruno, Lima Carolina Saldanha, Haydar Ahmed, Holanda Marcelo Alcantara, Hayashi Fatima Kiyoko, Ferreira Juliana Carvalho. (2025). Impact of a Competency-based Mechanical Ventilation Course Using Virtual Simulation. ATS Scholar. https://doi.org/10.34197/ats-scholar.2024-0083OC
title: Online competency-based mechanical ventilation course with virtual simulation (Xlung) for internal medicine residents
description: An 8-month online competency-based MV course built on 20 competencies adapted from a recommended MV competency guideline, organized into eight modules. Six modules combined a 1-hour live online meeting — "20 minutes of didactic lecture and 40 minutes for training using a virtual web-based simulator platform (Xlung)" — with self-directed learning material, retention quizzes, and Google Classroom delivery; two modules were exclusively self-directed. Engagement was reinforced through live meetings, an online platform, and group chats, and all residents received 1 month of deliberate simulator practice before the virtual SBA.
requirements: Access to the Xlung virtual simulator platform and Google Classroom
Live sessions limited to 1 hour, scheduled in the early evening to respect duty hours
constraints: Developed and delivered during the COVID-19 pandemic with all activities online
Two modules were exclusively self-directed without live simulation
target_learners: Internal medicine residents in a large university hospital residency program
target_learning_goals: Applying mechanical ventilation knowledge to simulated ICU scenarios across 20 MV competencies
examples: 81 of 103 residents completed the course, rating it effective with a net promoter score of 9.2
key_sources: Rocha de Macedo Bruno, Lima Carolina Saldanha, Haydar Ahmed, Holanda Marcelo Alcantara, Hayashi Fatima Kiyoko, Ferreira Juliana Carvalho. (2025). Impact of a Competency-based Mechanical Ventilation Course Using Virtual Simulation. ATS Scholar. https://doi.org/10.34197/ats-scholar.2024-0083OC
